question: Which group of people faces the highest risk of severe complications from food contamination?

options.A: Young adults with desk jobs
options.B: Teenagers playing sports
options.C: Young children and the elderly
options.D: Healthy middle-aged workers

explanation: Very young children and older adults have weaker immune systems, making it much harder for their bodies to fight off food poisoning. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h1)

question: What is the main goal of a patient referral system in reproductive health?

options.A: Connecting community-level needs with clinical care without losing patients in transit
options.B: Punishing healthcare workers who fail to meet monthly consultation targets
options.C: Ensuring every patient is admitted to a tertiary teaching hospital immediately
options.D: Tracking the financial profits of private maternity hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Referral systems make sure that when a patient needs more advanced care, they are safely guided to the right place without falling through the cracks. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T019#GNS226_U5_T019_h5)

question: What is the key difference between summarizing and synthesizing literature?

options.A: Grouping multiple studies together by themes and trends
options.B: Deleting any study that disagrees with your personal opinion
options.C: Copying abstracts word-for-word into your own paper
options.D: Listing every single article in strict chronological order

explanation: Synthesis means weaving different studies together around common themes, rather than just listing one summary after another. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T5#GNS217_U3_T5_h6)

question: What is the most important discharge instruction for a nurse to give a patient who just had a sigmoidoscopy with tissue biopsies?

options.A: Stay completely in bed until lab results come back.
options.B: Take strong pain pills to prevent soreness.
options.C: Report heavy bleeding or severe belly pain to the clinic right away.
options.D: Avoid solid food for two full days.

explanation: Spot on! Anytime tissue is sampled, patients must know which danger signs—like heavy bleeding or severe pain—mean they need to call the clinic. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T6#GNS221_U2_T6_h7)

question: Why can low levels of the brain chemical GABA lead to feeling more anxious?

options.A: GABA is responsible for speeding up heart rate during exercise.
options.B: GABA normally dampens neural activity, so a shortage leaves the brain overactive.
options.C: GABA produces the adrenaline needed to fight off physical infections.
options.D: GABA blocks serotonin from reaching the receptors in the brain.

explanation: GABA is your brain's natural chill pill! When you are short on it, your nerve cells keep firing away unchecked, leaving you feeling high-strung. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T10#GNS123_U3_T10_h2)

question: Which part of the ear does a tympanic thermometer aim for?

options.A: The sublingual pocket
options.B: The temporal artery
options.C: The tympanic membrane
options.D: The carotid sheath

explanation: Tympanic thermometers go gently into the ear canal to pick up heat coming straight off the eardrum. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h3)

question: What is the most immediate life-threatening complication of untreated, profuse watery diarrhea?

options.A: Hypovolemic shock from fluid loss
options.B: Enlargement of the liver and spleen
options.C: Permanent blockage of the colon
options.D: High blood pressure and stroke

explanation: Losing massive amounts of body fluid without adequate replacement drops blood volume dangerously low, leading to shock and organ failure. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h6)

question: Why is it hard to use raw numbers straight from a patient audit without descriptive statistics?

options.A: They are illegal to share within a hospital ward
options.B: They always contain mathematical calculation errors
options.C: They only apply to laboratory experiments
options.D: They are too overwhelming to spot patterns without organization

explanation: Think of raw data as a scattered mess of puzzle pieces. Without organizing them first, it's nearly impossible to spot trends or make sense of what's happening on the ward! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T2#GNS217_U4_T2_h1)

question: How is cholera primarily passed to humans?

options.A: Through direct skin-to-skin contact
options.B: Through contaminated water and food
options.C: By inhaling airborne respiratory droplets
options.D: Via the bite of infected mosquitoes

explanation: Swallowing water or food polluted with tiny traces of waste is how the bacteria enters our digestive system. Good hygiene stops it! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T18#GNS313_U2_T18_h2)

question: Why do nursing performance standards need to be clear and specific instead of vague?

options.A: Vague statements are illegal for hospitals to publish
options.B: Staff nurses refuse to read guidelines that contain descriptive words
options.C: Objective standards can be accurately measured and evaluated
options.D: Hospital accountants will not approve funding for subjective rules

explanation: When standards are clear and specific, every supervisor evaluates them the same way, making feedback fair and helpful. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h4)

question: A patient asks what happens to sperm immediately after they are created in the seminiferous tubules. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: They travel to the epididymis to mature.
options.B: They enter the prostate gland for activation.
options.C: They mix with urine in the urinary bladder.
options.D: They travel directly out through the penile skin.

explanation: After leaving the seminiferous tubules, sperm move into the duct system and head directly into the epididymis. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which professionals typically make up the multidisciplinary mental health team?

options.A: Surgeons, dentists, and hospital accountants
options.B: Lab technicians and administrative secretaries
options.C: Nurses, psychiatrists, social workers, and occupational therapists
options.D: Pharmacists and hospital security guards only

explanation: A comprehensive mental health team includes various specialists working together to address different recovery needs. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h7)

question: Morphine and digitalis are famous examples of drugs gotten from which natural source?

options.A: Minerals
options.B: Animals
options.C: Plants
options.D: Synthetic laboratories

explanation: You got it! Many powerful medicines we use today started out as active chemical extracts from plants. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T3#GNS125_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to help a patient move past a food myth?

options.A: Involving respected local community health volunteers
options.B: Acknowledging the good intentions behind the practice
options.C: Using simple analogies instead of heavy medical jargon
options.D: Directly insulting the patient's cultural background

explanation: Never insult a patient's heritage! It creates hostility and destroys the therapeutic nurse-patient relationship. Always keep your approach warm and respectful. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T017#GNS227_U2_T017_h6)

question: Which sensory receptors deep in the skin are great at detecting deep pressure and heavy vibrations?

options.A: Pacinian corpuscles
options.B: Free nerve endings
options.C: Meissner corpuscles
options.D: Merkel discs

explanation: Spot on! Pacinian corpuscles are shaped like tiny onions and sit deep in the skin to sense firm pressure and vibrations. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h7)

question: When is a 'competing' (directive) conflict style actually the right move in a hospital?

options.A: When discussing break schedules with colleagues
options.B: During emergency resuscitation or immediate safety threats
options.C: During routine morning shift handovers
options.D: When planning unit social events

explanation: In an emergency like a code blue, there's no time to debate. A strong leader needs to take charge immediately to keep the patient safe. [learn more](GST321_U5_T4#GST321_U5_T4_h5)

question: How do Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitors (INSTIs) stop HIV from multiplying?

options.A: By destroying red blood cells in the bloodstream
options.B: By preventing viral DNA from inserting into the host cell's DNA
options.C: By changing the patient's blood type permanently
options.D: By blocking the patient from feeling hungry

explanation: You got it! INSTIs block the 'integrase' enzyme, which the virus uses like glue to paste its own genetic code into our human cells. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T4#GNS216_U6_T4_h3)

question: What is the main job of a social worker on a community health team?

options.A: Reviewing lab results for abnormal electrolyte levels
options.B: Connecting families to housing and financial support
options.C: Performing surgical procedures in the clinic
options.D: Prescribing medications for high blood pressure

explanation: You got it! Social workers are pros at linking patients to resources outside the clinic that make daily life easier. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h3)

question: What is the primary reason patients with chronic malabsorption develop peripheral edema?

options.A: Loss of plasma proteins leading to decreased blood oncotic pressure
options.B: Direct blockage of the lymphatic vessels inside the lower extremities
options.C: Excessive retention of salt caused by overactive adrenal glands
options.D: Increased pumping pressure generated by a weakened heart muscle

explanation: When the gut fails to absorb protein, blood albumin drops. This lowers blood oncotic pressure, allowing fluid to leak out of vessels into body tissues. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h6)

question: Even though prolactin is high during pregnancy, why doesn't heavy milk production start right away?

options.A: Oxytocin suppresses milk synthesis until the baby is born
options.B: High levels of estrogen and progesterone block prolactin action
options.C: The alveoli are not yet fully formed until labor begins
options.D: The placenta actively destroys prolactin in the maternal blood

explanation: During pregnancy, the placenta keeps high levels of estrogen and progesterone around, which acts like a block on full milk production. Once the baby and placenta are delivered, that block lifts! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T17#GNS121_U5_T17_h2)

question: You gently pinch an elderly patient's forearm skin and notice it stays tented up for a few seconds before going down. What does this mean?

options.A: Dehydration or reduced skin elasticity
options.B: Excessive fluid retention in the subcutaneous tissue
options.C: Severe local skin inflammation or infection
options.D: Normal physiological response to warm ambient air

explanation: When skin stays up after pinching (poor turgor), it's a classic sign of low fluid levels (dehydration) or normal aging changes. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why do midwives use absorbable threads (sutures) for repairing perineal tears?

options.A: The body breaks them down naturally, so the mother doesn't need a visit just to remove stitches
options.B: They are the only threads that never cause allergies
options.C: They change color to warn you if an infection starts
options.D: They dissolve the second they touch warm water

explanation: Absorbable sutures save new mums the stress and discomfort of coming back to the clinic just to get stitches pulled out! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T10#GNS225_U3_T10_h5)

question: Why is it important to document whether the patient's pupils were dilated during the ophthalmoscopy?

options.A: It measures the exact neurological response speed of the brain
options.B: It explains how well the internal structures could be visualized
options.C: It prevents the next nurse from checking the visual acuity score
options.D: It proves that the correct eye drop dosage was billed to insurance

explanation: Pupillary dilation changes how much of the fundus is visible, so documenting dilation provides essential context for the examination findings. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h9)

question: Which of these is a key feature of institutional (hospital) care?

options.A: Complete client autonomy over daily schedules
options.B: Reliance solely on family members for medical tasks
options.C: A controlled and unfamiliar hospital setting
options.D: Delivery of services exclusively inside private homes

explanation: Correct! Institutional care happens in hospitals where routines and environments are strictly managed by the healthcare team. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is another name for a hospital-acquired infection?

options.A: Congenital disease
options.B: Chronic ailment
options.C: Idiopathic condition
options.D: Nosocomial infection

explanation: Infections caught while receiving medical care in a hospital or clinic are formally called nosocomial infections. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h1)

question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for in nursing communication?

options.A: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Action, Recovery
options.B: Safety, Behavior, Analysis, Response
options.C: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.D: Staffing, Bed availability, Assessment, Report

explanation: SBAR is a standardized framework used to structure verbal and written communication among healthcare professionals. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h6)

question: How do drug name stems help a student nurse understand unfamiliar medications?

options.A: They show the exact expiration date and proper storage temperature needed
options.B: They tell the nurse the exact retail price of the medication in the pharmacy
options.C: Common suffixes reveal the pharmacological class and general action of the drug
options.D: They indicate which manufacturing company produced the specific batch of pills

explanation: Drug stems (like '-olol' for beta-blockers) are like cheat codes! They tell you what family a drug belongs to, helping you guess its action even if you've never seen it before. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T8#GNS125_U1_T8_h2)

question: A patient with severe malaria isn't getting better despite finishing a full course of drugs bought from an unverified roadside vendor. What should you suspect?

options.A: The patient requires an immediate surgical intervention for appendicitis.
options.B: The hospital ward is experiencing an outbreak of a normal bacterial infection.
options.C: The patient's body has suddenly developed a lifelong immunity to all fevers.
options.D: The medication administered may be substandard or counterfeit.

explanation: When a trusted drug completely fails to work—especially from a shady source—always suspect that it might be a fake or low-quality product. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T1#GNS215_U1_T1_h6)

question: You need to continuously track both the baby's heart rate and the mother's contractions during a high-risk labour. Which tool do you grab?

options.A: Electronic fetal monitoring machine
options.B: Routine adult blood pressure cuff
options.C: Standard clinical mercury thermometer
options.D: Basic wooden fetoscope alone

explanation: Spot on! The EFM machine gives us a clear, non-stop picture of how the baby is handling contractions in real time. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h3)

question: Why are growth hormone and thyroid hormones so critical during infancy and childhood?

options.A: They regulate daily blood sugar levels after meals
options.B: They maintain normal calcium balance in the bones
options.C: They control the immediate fight-or-flight stress reaction
options.D: They coordinate normal skeletal growth and brain maturation

explanation: These two hormones work hand in hand to make sure a child's bones grow properly and their nervous system develops the way it should. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T5#GNS211_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which feature is a must-have for a true experimental research design?

options.A: Observation of natural behaviors
options.B: Random assignment of participants
options.C: Qualitative interview transcripts
options.D: Retrospective chart reviews

explanation: For an experiment to be truly 'true,' you need to randomly assign people to groups, actively change an independent variable, and have a control group to compare them against. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T1#GNS224_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which of these is a classic example of a biological agent?

options.A: A deficiency of protein in the diet
options.B: A bacterium causing a wound infection
options.C: Lead poisoning from old water pipes
options.D: Ultraviolet radiation from sunlight

explanation: Biological agents are living organisms like bacteria, viruses, or fungi that can cause infections. Great job keeping your categories straight! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T78#GNS214_U1_T78_h2)

question: When a patient is resting peacefully after a good meal, which part of their nervous system is hard at work?

options.A: Sympathetic division
options.B: Central integrative division
options.C: Parasympathetic division
options.D: Somatic motor division

explanation: Think 'rest and digest'! The parasympathetic system takes over when it's time to chill and recover energy. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is a major clinical safety concern when people use local herbal mixtures for family planning?

options.A: They are too expensive for rural community members
options.B: Modern clinics supply them free of charge
options.C: Lack of standardized dosing and potential toxicity
options.D: They always cause permanent surgical sterilization

explanation: Local herbal mixtures vary wildly in strength and ingredients, which can carry risks of accidental poisoning or harmful side effects. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T009#GNS226_U6_T009_h6)

question: What is the primary way many Nigerian patients currently pay for healthcare services?

options.A: Full government sponsorship
options.B: Free community charity funds
options.C: Out-of-pocket spending
options.D: Private international grants

explanation: A large portion of healthcare financing in Nigeria relies on direct out-of-pocket payments by individuals. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is the proper clinical term for unusually heavy or long menstrual periods?

options.A: Amenorrhea
options.B: Oligomenorrhea
options.C: Menorrhagia
options.D: Dysmenorrhea

explanation: Menorrhagia simply means heavy menstrual bleeding. As future nurses, we always watch out for this because it puts patients at risk for anemia. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T4#GNS121_U5_T4_h6)

question: Which of these is most likely to make people refuse to join a community insurance scheme?

options.A: A lack of trust in the managers handling the funds
options.B: Excessive availability of free medication
options.C: Too many doctors working in local health clinics
options.D: High levels of income among farmers

explanation: Trust is everything! If community members don't trust the people managing the money, they simply won't invest their hard-earned cash into the health scheme. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why is local health research important for nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Foreign textbooks are too expensive for local nursing students to buy
options.B: International organizations pay large grants exclusively to clinical nurses
options.C: Nigerian hospitals require every nurse to publish a paper before promotion
options.D: Western guidelines do not address specific local health challenges and cultural realities

explanation: You've got this! Local research matters because health issues like malaria management and maternal care need solutions tailored to our environment, rather than just copying foreign data. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the main danger if a patient suddenly stops taking their daily seizure medication?

options.A: It leads to complete kidney failure and lifelong dialysis needs
options.B: It causes immediate permanent blindness within a few hours
options.C: It results in rapid hair loss and severe skin pigmentation changes
options.D: It can trigger status epilepticus, a dangerous and prolonged seizure state

explanation: Stopping antiseizure drugs abruptly shocks the brain, causing a rebound effect that can trigger severe, continuous seizures (status epilepticus). Patients must always taper under medical advice! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T3#GNS223_U6_T3_h8)

question: What happens to bacteria when food is placed inside a properly working freezer?

options.A: They are instantly and fully killed.
options.B: Their reproduction stops completely.
options.C: They multiply faster in the cold air.
options.D: They turn into spores and fly away.

explanation: Freezing puts bacteria to sleep (dormant state), stopping them from multiplying, but it doesn't kill them completely. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h5)

question: Why is keeping strict privacy and confidentiality so important when teenagers come in for reproductive health services?

options.A: It removes the need to document clinical findings in health records
options.B: It is a legal requirement only for adult patients, not minors
options.C: It builds trust and encourages teens to seek necessary medical advice early
options.D: It prevents parents from ever knowing their child is growing up

explanation: You got it! Teens are often scared of being judged. Promising confidentiality helps them feel safe enough to get help before small issues turn big. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is a major danger of the social stigma surrounding abortion in healthcare?

options.A: Clients may delay seeking life-saving medical care out of fear
options.B: Hospital pharmacies automatically run out of emergency drugs
options.C: Infection rates drop because patients use home remedies first
options.D: Doctors are legally required to discharge patients within hours

explanation: Fear of harsh words or mistreatment often makes women wait too long to come to the hospital, which sadly makes their physical complications much worse. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h2)

question: What should you tell a patient about how much topical cream to use?

options.A: Apply a thick layer so it cures the condition faster
options.B: Use only the exact amount prescribed by the doctor
options.C: Stop using the cream as soon as symptoms disappear
options.D: Double the dose if the skin looks very dry or scaly

explanation: More isn't always better! Piling on extra cream won't speed up healing, but it can cause skin thinning and side effects. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T9#GNS122_U1_T9_h7)

question: What are the tiny, finger-like folds inside the small intestine that soak up all our nutrients called?

options.A: Villi
options.B: Sphincters
options.C: Haustra
options.D: Rugae

explanation: Brilliant! Villi (and their even tinier microvilli) create a massive surface area inside your small intestine so your body can absorb as many nutrients as possible. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T011#GNS227_U1_T011_h5)

question: What is the main goal of nursing research?

options.A: To reduce the number of working hours for staff
options.B: To develop trustworthy knowledge for the profession
options.C: To replace doctors in making medical diagnoses
options.D: To eliminate the need for clinical experience

explanation: Spot on! Nursing research is all about building a solid foundation of proven facts to make patient care better across the board. You've got this! [learn more](GNS217_U2_T4#GNS217_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why are awake COVID-19 patients sometimes asked to lie on their stomachs (prone positioning)?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for oxygen therapy
options.B: It makes it easier to insert nasogastric feeding tubes
options.C: It improves lung expansion and oxygen exchange
options.D: It prevents patients from developing pressure ulcers

explanation: Proning helps open up parts of the lungs that usually get squished, helping the patient breathe much better. Every day you're building clinical skills! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h5)

question: How can a nurse best handle personal biases when caring for a stigmatized patient?

options.A: Reading legal textbooks to punish patients who break social norms
options.B: Asking another nurse to handle all female reproductive health cases
options.C: Practicing active self-reflection and discussing feelings with supportive peers
options.D: Suppressing all emotions until the end of the calendar year

explanation: Talking things through with supportive colleagues and checking your own mindset helps you catch hidden biases before they affect your patient care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h7)

question: An 8-month-old baby is brought in with a cough and fast breathing. What sign tells you the baby needs antibiotics for pneumonia?

options.A: A slight decrease in daily milk intake
options.B: A clear nasal discharge and sneezing
options.C: Elevated respiratory rate for age while calm
options.D: A low-grade fever that responds to tepid sponging

explanation: Correct! Fast breathing while the baby is calm is a key clinical sign of lower respiratory infections like pneumonia. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T2#GNS225_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why might a multi-million-dollar MRI machine be considered inappropriate technology for a rural primary health clinic?

options.A: Rural patients do not have brains or spinal cords to scan
options.B: Magnetic machines are forbidden by traditional cultural beliefs
options.C: The clinic lacks reliable electricity, trained technicians, and repair parts
options.D: The government prefers traditional herbs over digital imaging

explanation: Advanced machinery fails the test of appropriateness if the local setting lacks the infrastructure and support to keep it running. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of filling out an incident report?

options.A: To provide direct evidence for firing the nurse on duty
options.B: To permanently record patient complaints for the police
options.C: To record the facts of an unexpected event so the system can learn from it
options.D: To increase the patient's hospital bill for the extra care needed

explanation: Incident reports are safety tools used to track problems and improve hospital systems, not punitive write-ups. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h5)

question: What happens to oxygen and carbon dioxide levels in the body during asphyxia?

options.A: High nitrogen and low carbon dioxide
options.B: Low nitrogen and high oxygen
options.C: High oxygen and low carbon dioxide
options.D: Low oxygen and high carbon dioxide

explanation: Think of asphyxia as a double hit: oxygen drops while carbon dioxide builds up rapidly in the blood because the body cannot get rid of it. You've got this! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T6#GNS221_U3_T6_h1)

question: A patient falls ill with typhoid after drinking contaminated water. What type of transmission is this?

options.A: Vector-borne transmission
options.B: Indirect transmission
options.C: Airborne transmission
options.D: Direct transmission

explanation: You got it! Because the water acted as a vehicle between the source and the patient, it counts as indirect transmission. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T1#GNS313_U2_T1_h3)

question: A patient is struggling with balance and feeling dizzy often. Which nerve is likely acting up?

options.A: Optic nerve
options.B: Olfactory nerve
options.C: Vestibulocochlear nerve
options.D: Trochlear nerve

explanation: You nailed it! The vestibulocochlear nerve (CN VIII) helps us keep our balance and stay steady on our feet. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T15#GNS211_U3_T15_h2)

question: Why do community nurses take their analyzed data back to the community for validation?

options.A: To hide negative health statistics from government officials
options.B: To punish local residents who refused to answer survey questions
options.C: To confirm the accuracy of findings with the community members
options.D: To print extra copies of the survey questionnaire

explanation: Validation is all about checking your homework with the people who live there to make sure your conclusions match their everyday reality. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T2#GNS124_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why are Insecticide-Treated Nets (ITNs) most effective when used while sleeping?

options.A: Anopheles mosquitoes bite mostly at night when people are asleep
options.B: It prevents mosquitoes from laying eggs inside household water pots
options.C: The chemical on the net repels daytime flies and cockroaches
options.D: It completely stops the flow of humid air into the bedroom

explanation: You got it! Since malaria mosquitoes love to hunt during the night, sleeping under a treated net hits them right when they are most active. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T3#GNS214_U1_T3_h6)

question: You notice clear fluid draining from the nose of a patient who just had pituitary surgery. What is a quick bedside test to see if it is cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)?

options.A: Smell the fluid to check for a sharp ammonia or vinegar odor.
options.B: Check the exact temperature of the fluid with a digital probe.
options.C: Shine an ultraviolet light directly onto the wet dressing.
options.D: Test the fluid for glucose using a standard urine dipstick.

explanation: CSF is rich in glucose, whereas normal nasal mucus is not! Touching a glucose test strip to the drainage is a fast, clever way at the bedside to check for a CSF leak. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T9#GNS222_U2_T9_h8)

question: You notice women in a village want birth control but are scared of their husbands' reactions. What should be your main step?

options.A: Give out contraceptives in secret without telling anyone
options.B: Report all the husbands to the nearest police station
options.C: Organize community talks to involve men in reproductive health education
options.D: Close the clinic until the village changes its culture

explanation: Brilliant approach! Bringing men into the conversation clears up myths, reduces home conflicts, and builds teamwork for family health. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h7)

question: Why should a nurse recommend locally available foods during dietary counselling?

options.A: It ensures the family can afford and sustain the dietary advice
options.B: Government policies ban the use of foreign food items
options.C: Local foods require no cooking or preparation time
options.D: Imported foods are always toxic to young children

explanation: Good nursing advice must be practical! Recommending local foods ensures the family can actually afford and keep up with the diet. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h8)

question: What is the main reason for scheduling follow-up visits after dietary counselling?

options.A: Punishing patients who failed to follow their meal plan
options.B: Re-assessing baseline anthropometric data from scratch every week
options.C: Charging additional consultation fees for hospital revenue
options.D: Monitoring progress, reviewing food logs, and adjusting goals

explanation: Right! Follow-ups let us celebrate wins, talk through struggles, and tweak the plan so it keeps working for the patient. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h7)

question: What is the main building block the body uses to make steroid hormones?

options.A: Glucose
options.B: Tyrosine
options.C: Cholesterol
options.D: Hemoglobin

question: Why might a clinic suddenly record a higher incidence of a disease after getting a brand-new testing machine?

question: What is the main job of white blood cells when an infection enters the body?

question: Which handy tool do nurses use to track changes in a patient's level of consciousness?

question: Why must a nurse check a female patient's surgical history before placing an IV in her arm?

question: Why do nurses rush to give IV fluids mainly to protect the 'zone of stasis' in a burn?

question: A nursing lecturer uses a physical heart model to explain blood flow to students with different learning styles. Which group benefits most from handling and examining this model directly?

options.C: Visual learners

question: What are the normal blood vessels found inside a healthy newborn umbilical cord?

question: Which of these means a planned home birth is definitely NOT safe?

question: Why is using misoprostol by itself very common in areas with limited healthcare resources?

question: What is the main goal of preparing a modified-texture diet for a patient with swallowing difficulties (dysphagia)?

question: Besides relieving pressure, what is another major reason for doing a paracentesis?

question: Why do working nurses need continuous professional development (CPD) programs?

options.C: Hospital management needs a way to reduce staff salary budgets
options.D: Medical knowledge and clinical technology change over time

explanation: Medicine never stays still! CPD helps nurses stay updated with new life-saving techniques, equipment, and medical knowledge throughout their careers. [learn more](GST321_U4_T1#GST321_U4_T1_h4)

question: After a diagnostic laparoscopy, a patient complains of sharp shoulder pain. What is likely going on?

question: In a reflex arc, which part carries the nerve impulse away from the central nervous system?

question: How is a vasospasm different from atherosclerosis?

options.A: Vasospasm only affects veins, while atherosclerosis affects capillaries

options.C: Vasospasm takes decades to form, whereas plaque forms in seconds

explanation: A vasospasm is just a sudden, temporary twitch or squeeze of the muscle in the blood vessel wall. Atherosclerosis, on the other hand, is a long-term buildup of fatty gunk. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T10#GNS213_U1_T10_h2)

question: What is a key everyday duty for health workers when it comes to food policy?

question: Where does a boat (or maritime) nurse primarily work?

question: What is the main reason for setting clear, measurable goals in a health plan?

question: How does high resistance in the body's blood vessels affect the heart?

options.C: It lowers the heart rate by relaxing the nervous system

question: Why is the enforcement of laws against forced marriage sometimes challenging in Nigeria?

question: After finishing passive exercises for an unconscious patient, what is the final safety step you must take?

question: How does gastroenteritis fundamentally affect the gastrointestinal tract?

question: Which gas law explains why trapped air inside a patient's body expands as an aircraft climbs?

question: Which condition is a speech-language pathologist specially trained to evaluate and treat?

question: Which nutrient is especially important for a new mother to help prevent severe tiredness and anemia?

question: A patient has been on a strict low-fat diet for months. Which sign might point to a vitamin deficiency?

question: Why must certain antiretroviral drugs be taken alongside food?

question: What is the nurse's specific job when handling a surgical consent form?

question: How does cigarette smoking increase the risk of developing vulval tumours?

question: Why is it best to combine mass media with face-to-face counselling in health campaigns?

question: What is the main job of the endocrine system in our body?

question: Why does breastfeeding usually demand more energy and nutrition from a mother than pregnancy did?

question: How do we classify used surgical blades and needles in the hospital?

question: Which management style best reflects the psychology part of Deming's framework?

question: Why is building a trusting relationship especially important during home health visits?

question: What is the main job of the government when working in partnership with NGOs?

options.A: Setting national policies and regulatory oversight
options.B: Manufacturing all global vaccines
options.C: Managing private donor bank accounts
options.D: Handling daily fundraising events abroad

question: A patient scheduled for a spinal tap is currently taking warfarin for a heart condition. What is the nurse's best action?

options.A: Notify the doctor immediately about the bleeding risk
options.B: Proceed with the tap quickly before the next drug dose
options.C: Apply a hot pack to the lower back to thin the blood
options.D: Encourage the patient to drink extra water right away

question: As a healthy newborn baby grows into a strong child, how do their muscles mostly grow?

options.A: Conversion of fat tissue into skeletal muscle
options.B: Constant destruction and replacement of fibers
options.C: Hypertrophy of existing muscle fibers
options.D: Continuous division of new muscle cells

explanation: Since we are born with most of the muscle fibers we'll ever have, childhood growth happens because those existing fibers get thicker and longer (hypertrophy). Simple and fascinating! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T8#GNS121_U3_T8_h4)

question: As a midwife checking the lower boundary of the pelvic cavity, which bones help form the pelvic outlet?

options.B: Ischial tuberosities and coccyx
options.C: Linea terminalis and sacral ala
options.D: Iliac crests and sacral promontory

explanation: Think of the bottom exit of the pelvis: it's bounded by your tailbone (coccyx), the sitting bones (ischial tuberosities), and the front pubic bone. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h4)

question: A patient is admitted with suspected infective endocarditis. Which test is best for directly viewing the valve growths?

options.A: Standard 12-lead ECG
options.B: Chest X-ray
options.C: Echocardiogram
options.D: Complete blood count

explanation: An echocardiogram uses sound waves (like an ultrasound for the heart) to let doctors actually see those moving valve growths clearly. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why must a nursing operational plan be kept simple?

options.A: So that every member of the healthcare team can easily understand and follow it.
options.B: So managers do not have to explain the plan during meetings.
options.C: Because complex medical terms confuse hospital accountants.
options.D: To make sure the planning document fits onto a single page.

explanation: If a plan is overly complicated, busy nurses and staff will misunderstand the steps. Simple plans keep everyone on the same page! [learn more](GST321_U1_T7#GST321_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a main goal for a community nurse working to prevent disease?

options.A: Promoting local participation in mass immunization campaigns
options.B: Enforcing mandatory fines for community members who refuse treatment
options.C: Teaching residents how to identify and clear mosquito breeding sites
options.D: Educating families on safe food storage and personal hygiene habits

explanation: Nurses are educators, caregivers, and advocates. Handing out fines and police enforcement is up to legal authorities, not the nursing team! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h7)

question: Which nursing action is most important during an arthrocentesis procedure?

options.A: Walking the patient around the room
options.B: Maintaining a strict sterile field
options.C: Massaging the joint vigorously with bare hands
options.D: Giving the patient strong oral pain pills

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important for a maternal near-miss survivor?

options.A: It prevents her from developing high blood pressure in future years
options.B: Mental health counseling helps her uterus contract back to normal size
options.C: She is at high risk for post-traumatic stress disorder and depression
options.D: Psychological therapy is required to restore normal blood hemoglobin levels

explanation: Coming that close to death leaves deep emotional scars. Checking in on her mental well-being is just as important as checking her physical vitals! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T013#GNS226_U1_T013_h7)

question: Why do nurses need to be extra careful when giving sleeping pills to older adult patients?

options.A: Older adults process drugs faster, rendering the pills useless
options.B: Sleeping pills increase the risk of daytime drowsiness and accidental falls
options.C: Older adults are legally barred from taking sleeping medications
options.D: Sedatives always cause severe allergic reactions in senior patients

explanation: Sedatives can linger in an older adult's system, causing grogginess and unsteady legs during the day. This puts them at high risk for falls! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h6)

question: How can a severe infection in the middle ear or sinuses end up causing a brain abscess?

options.A: By traveling directly through the bloodstream via the auditory nerve sheath
options.B: By causing systemic dehydration that concentrates bacteria in brain tissue
options.C: By eroding through adjacent thin cranial bones into the central nervous system
options.D: By triggering an autoimmune response that attacks the cerebral cortex

explanation: The bone walls separating your sinuses and ears from your brain are surprisingly thin. A severe, unchecked infection can literally wear right through that bone and spread to the brain. Fascinating and crucial to know! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h8)

question: What happens to a regular medication when 'enzyme induction' speeds up its breakdown?

options.A: It blocks the drug from ever entering the gastrointestinal tract
options.B: It raises the blood concentration of the drug to toxic levels instantly
options.C: It lowers the blood concentration of the drug by speeding up its breakdown
options.D: It turns the active drug into a permanent fat-soluble storage molecule

explanation: Induction basically creates a 'night shift' of extra enzymes. They clear out the drug so fast that the medication levels drop below what's needed to help the patient—hello, treatment failure! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T3#GNS125_U5_T3_h6)

question: What is the main result you look for in a qualitative thematic analysis?

options.A: A laboratory value chart for patient diagnostics
options.B: A bar graph showing demographic frequency counts
options.C: Overarching themes that capture the meaning of the data
options.D: A precise statistical correlation coefficient

explanation: You're doing great! Thematic analysis groups all the interview notes into big, meaningful themes that tell the core story of the research. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T5#GNS224_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why should you always teach your patients the difference between a normal side effect and a dangerous adverse reaction?

options.A: It prevents panic over normal symptoms while ensuring prompt reporting of dangerous signs
options.B: It eliminates the need for any follow-up visits with the primary doctor
options.C: It guarantees the patient will never experience any drug discomfort
options.D: It allows the patient to legally prescribe their own antidote medications

explanation: Mild drowsiness is okay, but throat swelling is an emergency! Teaching the difference keeps patients calm and safe. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h5)

question: In James Reason's famous Swiss cheese model of safety, what do the holes in the cheese represent?

options.A: The exact time a medication is due
options.B: Gaps in nursing school curriculum
options.C: The total number of patients admitted to a ward
options.D: Weaknesses in individual safety defense layers

explanation: Think of each cheese slice as a safety barrier. The holes are just the temporary cracks or flaws in those defenses. [learn more](GST319_U5_T4#GST319_U5_T4_h2)

question: During a home visit, a nurse sees a parole patient acting paranoid, talking to unseen things, and throwing away meds. What is the nurse's priority?

options.A: Tell the patient's neighbors to handle the situation.
options.B: Report it to the care team right away to prevent a full relapse.
options.C: Wait three weeks until the next scheduled doctor visit.
options.D: Ignore it since the patient is living outside the hospital now.

question: Which of these is a vital disease-prevention shot routinely given during pregnancy clinics in Nigeria?

options.A: Insulin pump placement
options.B: Tetanus toxoid vaccination
options.C: Chemotherapy infusion
options.D: Joint replacement surgery

explanation: Well done! Tetanus toxoid is a routine life-saver given during pregnancy to protect both the mother and newborn baby from tetanus. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h2)

question: What is the key symptom that helps differentiate abruptio placentae from placenta praevia?

options.A: Complete absence of any bleeding
options.B: Presence of severe abdominal pain
options.C: Bright red color of the blood
options.D: Onset of bleeding before 24 weeks

question: Which medication is the main choice for treating onchocerciasis?

options.A: Ivermectin
options.B: Penicillin
options.C: Chloroquine
options.D: Quinine

explanation: Ivermectin is the superstar drug used worldwide to clear out microfilariae and protect people's sight. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T7#GNS214_U1_T7_h5)

question: A patient comes in with ringworm on their arm. What type of germ causes this common skin condition?

options.A: Fungi
options.B: Parasite
options.C: Bacteria
options.D: Virus

explanation: Correct! Don't let the name fool you—ringworm is caused by a fungus, not an actual worm. It loves warm, damp skin spots! [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is a major advantage of using topical NSAIDs instead of oral NSAIDs for older adults with osteoarthritis?

options.A: They never require a prescription from a doctor
options.B: They work within seconds to stop all joint swelling
options.C: They completely reverse the loss of joint cartilage

explanation: Topical NSAIDs deliver medicine directly to the painful joint through the skin, avoiding the high bloodstream concentrations that cause gastrointestinal bleeding. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h5)

question: Why do many patients feel shoulder pain shortly after laparoscopic gallbladder surgery?

options.A: Trapped carbon dioxide gas irritating the phrenic nerve
options.B: Muscle strain from lifting heavy things too early
options.C: Infection in the shoulder joint from bad positioning
options.D: Direct nerve damage from surgical tools

explanation: You've got this! The gas used to inflate the belly during surgery can irritate the diaphragm, causing a weird referred pain up in the shoulder. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h6)

question: How do occupational health programs differ from regular hospital care?

options.A: They only handle severe physical trauma and surgeries
options.B: They focus heavily on prevention and work environments
options.C: They ignore mental health and focus strictly on machinery
options.D: They are managed exclusively by financial auditors

explanation: While hospitals treat people after they fall sick, occupational health steps in early to make the workplace itself safe so illnesses never happen in the first place. Makes total sense, right? [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of a research design in nursing?

options.A: To calculate the final cost of the research project
options.B: To replace the need for an institutional review board
options.C: To format the bibliography of a research paper
options.D: To act as a blueprint for answering a clinical question

explanation: Think of a research design like an architectural blueprint. It gives you a clear, step-by-step plan to follow so you can find accurate answers to your clinical questions! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T1#GNS224_U1_T1_h1)

question: What usually triggers a flexor or withdrawal reflex?

options.A: An increase in body temperature during physical exercise
options.B: A painful stimulus such as stepping on a sharp object
options.C: A sudden stretch caused by lifting a heavy object
options.D: A gentle tap on a tendon to test joint movement

explanation: Flexor reflexes are our automatic survival responses. When something hurts—like stepping on a pin—you pull away before you even have time to think about it. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T27#GNS211_U3_T27_h4)

question: Why do doctors check blood calcium and PTH levels at the same time?

options.A: To determine if the thyroid gland is producing too much thyroxine

options.C: To calculate the exact glomerular filtration rate of both kidneys
options.D: To see if the parathyroid gland's hormone response matches the calcium level

explanation: Comparing PTH and calcium together helps clinicians figure out if a calcium problem is actually coming from a misbehaving parathyroid gland. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T11#GNS222_U2_T11_h6)

question: What happens to the nerve in a mild injury called neurapraxia?

options.A: The axon stays intact while the myelin sheath suffers temporary damage
options.B: The blood supply to the nerve is permanently cut off, causing rapid cell death
options.C: Both the axon and the outer connective tissue sheaths are completely severed
options.D: The axon is crushed or cut while the outer connective tissue tube stays intact

question: What is the main goal of giving someone a vaccine?

options.A: To provide temporary ready-made antibodies that last for one week
options.B: To physically block viruses from entering the body through the skin
options.C: To destroy all normal bacteria living inside the gastrointestinal tract
options.D: To stimulate memory cell production without causing severe disease

explanation: Vaccines introduce safe pieces of a germ so your immune system can build memory cells without you getting sick. [learn more](GST114_U4_T5#GST114_U4_T5_h8)

question: When someone pushes back against your advocacy campaign, which of these should you NOT do?

options.A: Dismissing the critic's concerns as foolish and uneducated
options.B: Anticipating counter-arguments ahead of time with solid data
options.C: Acknowledging their point of view respectfully before pivoting
options.D: Remaining calm, professional, and prepared with evidence

question: Why is Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA) so helpful in primary healthcare clinics across Nigeria?

options.A: It completely cures any existing viral infection within a few minutes

question: Why are typhoid and paratyphoid fevers grouped together as 'enteric fevers'?

question: What is the main goal of giving someone a vaccine?

options.A: To stimulate antibody production and memory cell formation without causing disease

options.C: To permanently destroy all innate immune system pathways
options.D: To provide immediate relief from acute bacterial infections

question: Why is poor sanitation a major risk factor for catching amoebiasis?

options.B: Poor waste management makes the air toxic to human lungs

question: Why can taking an oral azole antifungal cause other routine medications to become toxic in the body?

question: What is the term for an infection that jumps naturally between animals and humans?

question: How does catching a larger amount (dose) of germs affect the incubation period?

question: Up to what gestational age is MVA typically performed in the first trimester?

question: What hormone stimulates the gallbladder to contract and release bile into the small intestine?

question: What dangerous practice must nurses avoid to protect themselves from needlestick injuries?

question: Why might a patient with a ruptured ectopic pregnancy feel pain in her shoulder?

question: What should you do as a nurse at a primary clinic if a patient walks in with a complication you cannot handle?

options.C: Stabilize the patient, write a referral letter, and contact the receiving facility
options.D: Ignore the complication since primary clinics handle all cases

question: A patient has severe liver disease. Which part of drug processing will most likely be affected?

question: Where is the best place on an infant's body to give an intramuscular (IM) injection?

question: How do automated smart beds help prevent pressure sores?

question: Which of the following is a classic physical sign of repeated abuse often seen during a nursing assessment?

question: What main feature defines a traditional community in public health?

options.D: A shared geographic boundary and common interests

question: Why does the government bother controlling and monitoring health spending?

options.C: To replace traditional medicine with imported drugs
options.D: To manage limited resources and prevent financial waste

question: If a patient casually mentions they drink a lot of alcohol when you ask about social habits, what should be your first nursing reaction?

options.B: Acknowledge the disclosure calmly without showing judgment
options.C: Immediately document that the patient has an addiction
options.D: Scold the patient for damaging their liver health

question: Which of these shows a patient is having trouble with the ADL of 'transferring'?

options.A: The patient forgets to add sugar to their tea.

options.C: The patient wears mismatched socks and unbuttoned shirts.

question: What is the minimum number of generations a nurse should typically explore when taking a family health history?

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical role of the nurse during the implementation phase?

options.C: Acting as a strict dictator who punishes lazy workers

question: A patient complains of mild tummy cramping and bloating shortly after a colonoscopy. What is the usual cause?

question: What is a major goal of any good pharmacovigilance program?

options.C: Lowering the market price of essential pharmaceutical goods
options.D: Replacing traditional clinical trials with computer simulations

question: Which term describes healthcare that fully respects a patient's personal preferences and values?

options.A: Resource efficiency
options.B: Patient-centeredness
options.C: Technological automation
options.D: Institutional rigidity

question: Why should nurses avoid vague phrases like 'skin looks infected' in professional charting?

options.C: It automatically violates hospital legal policies regarding privacy protection

question: If a needle has a lower gauge number, what does that tell you about its size?

question: How long must you listen with a stethoscope in a single part of the tummy before you can safely write down that there are 'no bowel sounds'?

question: Which of these is NOT a factor contributing to high maternal mortality in Nigeria?

options.D: High levels of poverty and malnutrition

question: How do calcimimetic medications help treat hyperparathyroidism?

question: Why is it so tricky to spot an asymptomatic carrier during a disease outbreak?

question: You are caring for a 38-week pregnant mother with many past deliveries who also has severe anemia. What is the best delivery recommendation?

question: What common, mild-sounding urinary issue during pregnancy can turn into a serious kidney infection (pyelonephritis) if ignored?

question: How many pairs of spinal nerves are in the human body?

question: A patient with a chest stab wound suddenly loses their pulse and shows PEA (pulseless electrical activity) on the monitor. What is the best immediate action?

question: What is the teach-back method used for during patient education?

question: Which imaging scan is usually best for getting a detailed look at the tiny pituitary gland?

question: Which group of workers faces the highest daily risk of exposure to bloodborne infections like HIV and Hepatitis B?

question: Why does injured skin become extra sensitive (hyperalgesia) after a burn?

question: What is one of the earliest warning signs of hidden blood loss or developing shock?

question: Why can't we use heavy weights in skin traction?

question: Why can tubal damage from salpingitis lead to an ectopic pregnancy?

question: Which type of medication starts at Step 1 of the WHO pain ladder for mild pain?

question: What is the most important thing for a nurse to check right after giving a nebulizer treatment with a beta-agonist?

question: When should a nurse question a doctor's order to start systemic corticosteroid therapy?

question: What is the primary purpose of a professional nursing organization?

question: A 5-year-old child with a heavy roundworm infection has vomiting, colicky tummy pain, and a sausage-like lump felt in the belly. What is the most likely complication?

question: Which chemical exposure patient needs to be rushed straight to the resuscitation bay?

question: Why are greenstick fractures much more common in young children than in adults?

question: What generally happens to the tracheostomy hole (stoma) after the tube is permanently removed?

question: Why is it best for nurses to avoid using extreme scare tactics when talking to teens about drugs?

options.A: Teens prefer lectures over friendly conversations
options.B: Exaggerated warnings are required by medical law
options.C: Teenagers see right through exaggerated claims and may lose trust in the nurse
options.D: Scare tactics instantly cure physical dependence within hours

explanation: Correct! Exaggerated warnings destroy your credibility. Teens spot fake claims easily, and once they lose trust, they stop listening altogether. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T13#GNS312_U3_T13_h6)

question: Which action shows a nursing manager applying great leadership on a busy ward?

options.A: Punishing nurses publicly whenever a minor documentation error occurs
options.B: Making all clinical decisions alone without consulting the care team
options.C: Ignoring staff complaints about burnout to focus only on budgets
options.D: Listening to shift concerns and fighting for adequate staffing resources

explanation: A great manager has their team's back. Listening to burnout concerns and fighting for enough hands on deck keeps both nurses and patients safe and happy. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why should nurses use open-ended questions when talking to a child about an injury?

options.A: To avoid leading the child and contaminating potential legal evidence
options.B: To speed up the clinical assessment process during busy shifts
options.C: To comply with hospital billing guidelines for pediatric trauma
options.D: To encourage the child to blame their siblings instead of parents

explanation: Asking leading questions puts words in the child's mouth, which ruins the reliability of any future legal investigation. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T24#GNS225_U5_T24_h5)

question: Why are the three semicircular canals placed at right angles to each other?

options.A: To make room for the auditory nerve inside the skull
options.B: To detect rotational movement in all three spatial dimensions
options.C: To allow equal pressure distribution of perilymph fluid
options.D: To prevent the endolymph from flowing too quickly

explanation: This clever layout lets your brain pick up movement in every direction: up and down, side to side, and tilting! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h2)

question: What makes farming pesticides particularly dangerous in rural areas?

options.A: Farmers use them exclusively as food flavoring agents in local dishes
options.B: They are frequently stored near food items and handled without protective gear
options.C: They only affect animals and have zero toxic impact on human physiology
options.D: They lose their toxicity completely within a few minutes of application

explanation: Spot on! When chemicals are kept close to food and used without gloves or masks, accidental poisoning happens easily. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h2)

question: Why is it so tricky to make drugs that kill parasites without harming human patients?

options.A: Parasites share a similar eukaryotic cell structure with human hosts
options.B: Human immune systems cannot produce antibodies against parasites
options.C: Parasites replicate much faster than bacterial pathogens
options.D: Antiparasitic medications are always destroyed by stomach acid

explanation: You've got this! Because both human cells and parasites are eukaryotic (complex cells with a nucleus), it's tough to design a medicine that attacks the parasite without hurting our own cells. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h1)

question: If a patient scrapes the surface of their skin without a deep cut, which layer took the hit?

options.A: Subcutaneous fat layer
options.B: Skeletal muscle
options.C: Hypodermis
options.D: Stratum corneum

explanation: Correct! The stratum corneum is the very top layer of the epidermis, meaning it handles all the daily friction and minor scrapes. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT normal and actually represents a danger sign in a newborn?

options.A: Passing dark green meconium poop on the first day
options.B: Grunting when breathing and chest sinking in
options.C: Spitting up a tiny bit of milk after feeding
options.D: Sleeping soundly between regular feeds

explanation: Chest retractions and grunting are red flags! They tell us the baby is working way too hard to breathe and needs urgent help. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h9)

question: Why does Lassa fever spike during the dry season?

options.A: Farming activities and bush burning drive rats closer to homes
options.B: Cold weather lowers human immune systems significantly
options.C: Increased humidity allows the virus to spread faster in the air
options.D: Heavy rainfall causes stagnant water to breed the virus

explanation: When fields are cleared and burned, the rats lose their natural habitat and move straight into grain stores and residential areas. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T8#GNS214_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to communicate without judgment when assessing these patients?

options.A: It prevents the hospital from paying for laboratory investigations
options.B: It encourages the patient to truthfully share what methods were used, aiding proper treatment
options.C: It guarantees the patient will never experience physical pain
options.D: It is required by criminal law enforcement agencies in all Nigerian states

explanation: When patients feel judged, they hide details like chemical use or instrument trauma. A warm, welcoming attitude saves lives! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h6)

question: Which three systems work together to keep our body balanced and steady?

options.A: Digestive, endocrine, and skeletal systems
options.B: Respiratory, circulatory, and nervous systems
options.C: Vestibular, visual, and proprioceptive systems
options.D: Lymphatic, integumentary, and muscular systems

explanation: Your body is amazing! It coordinates signals from your inner ears, eyes, and body sensors to keep you steady without you even thinking about it. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h1)

question: How does long-term release of cortisol help the body cope with extended stress?

options.A: By increasing available blood glucose and energy supplies
options.B: By lowering the heart rate and blood pressure to rest
options.C: By promoting rapid storage of extra body fat in muscles
options.D: By enhancing digestion and nutrient absorption in the gut

explanation: Cortisol breaks down stored fats and proteins to keep your blood sugar up, ensuring your body has plenty of energy to push through tough, stressful times. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T5#GNS211_U1_T5_h7)
